_README: The CLOSED set of build inputs the release may consume from shared mutable state.
next build bakes NEXT_PUBLIC_* into the client bundle, so the same commit can produce different
artifacts depending on what those variables held at build time. Binding them is what makes
'same commit' imply 'same artifact'. Their VALUES are already public by construction -- they ship to
every browser -- so recording them discloses nothing that is not already shipped.
WHAT IS READ, PRECISELY. The generator parses the release's env files, selects ONLY assignments whose
name begins NEXT_PUBLIC_, and records nothing else. No other variable name and no other value enters
the receipt, any log, or any error message.
The set is CLOSED: a NEXT_PUBLIC_* variable present at build time but absent from this allowlist
blocks publication, so a new build input cannot appear silently. An allowlisted name that is absent
at build time is not an error -- these are permissions, not requirements.

allowed.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_ENABLE_HATE_CRIME
allowed.detail: Feature flag for the Hate Crime source. The deploy already refuses to build unless it is exactly true or false, because a missing flag silently produces wrong client behaviour. Baked into the client bundle.

allowed.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL
allowed.detail: Public base URL used by client-side code. Baked into the client bundle.
